answer: In an agent economy, require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before it can submit bids, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fraud. A single operator can still create many identities, but each one ties up capital and risks losing it, so flooding the market is costly rather than free. Auditors can compare behavior across a vertex of agents, tracing a river of coordinated bids across the tundra to prioritize review; the bond, not the metaphor, makes the attack expensive.
